`decide.py open` requires `--plan` (argparse required=True), with `--force` as the only escape hatch for a question that has no real governing plan doc yet ("creates an orphan node"). J-1199 (a build job with `plan: null` in its own job-queue entry -- ordinary and precedented, findings.jsonl/decisions.jsonl already carry plan:null rows) hit this directly when raising D-0252: the only way to file it was `--force --plan lab_isolation` against a slug with no matching docs/plans or docs/staged file. That works, but it means every plan-less founder question either becomes a same-named "orphan" plan slug (noise for plan-index/plan-liveness, which scan docs/plans + docs/staged and would never resolve it) or gets silently left out of the ledger entirely by a more cautious caller. A dedicated sentinel (e.g. `--plan none` mapping to a real `null`, distinct from an orphan slug) would let plan-index/plan-liveness/decide-review tell "genuinely plan-less" apart from "typo'd or not-yet-written plan doc" without any caller needing --force.

Worth a check (in job_queue.py add/spawn, or a lint pass) that flags a mismatch when a briefing contains the literal phrase ISOLATION REQUIRED but the isolation field is not required/lab_env, the same way plan-schema-audit already flags missing required fields.

job-run's per-job worktree isolation doesn't cover docs/staged/*.md plan-doc updates the way it covers code: J-1220's own worktree (wt_chapter_id_repair, base commit b3eb8bc = current master at dispatch) has docs/staged/chapter_id_repair.md ending at the D-0251/J-1197-spawn section (100 lines) -- it is MISSING the two most-recent "Current State" sections (J-1197/F-1704's census, J-1217/F-1715's build) that are visible in C:\Nascence's own LIVE working tree right now, but only as an UNCOMMITTED modification (git status at this conversation's start showed "M docs/staged/chapter_id_repair.md", not a commit). Since b3eb8bc is HEAD, those two sections were apparently never actually committed to master -- whoever wrote them (presumably J-1197/J-1217's own sessions) edited the shared C:\Nascence tree directly for this file, rather than their own worktree copies the way code files are handled (e.g. core/essay_lesson.py's own changes DID land as real commits, 71f967b etc). Net effect: any job dispatched into a fresh worktree after that point (like J-1220) silently gets an OLDER snapshot of this specific file than what's live in the shared tree, and appending a new section "at the end" of the worktree's own copy places it BEFORE those two uncommitted sections once/if they're ever committed -- a real risk of an out-of-order doc or a content-level merge conflict at the next worktree-merge step, for THIS file specifically (not code). Worth a documented convention (either: plan-doc Current State edits should also go through a real worktree+commit like code does, or the merge step should specifically 3-way-merge docs/staged/*.md content rather than assume a clean git merge will suffice) rather than leaving it to be rediscovered per-job. plan_files_audit.py's extract_refs() (imported unchanged by plan_liveness.py) mis-cites docs/job_queue.jsonl as an "evidence file" for geometry_tuple_index -- the current docs/reviews/plan_liveness_audit.md shows it GATE-MET+UNREAD (1233 rows vs threshold 210) for this plan, which is nonsensical: job_queue.jsonl is the toolchain's own job queue, not a Nascence evidence log. Root cause: docs/staged/geometry_tuple_index.md section 11 "WHERE IT SITS" mentions the filename in passing -- "docs/job_queue.jsonl J-0210 (the real, independently-filed, actionable first step this whole document is downstream of)" -- a citation to a job ID, not a claim that the queue file itself backs this plan. extract_refs()'s regex has no way to distinguish "this file is our evidence" from "see job J-0210, logged in this file, for context." Same false-positive family as the threshold-parsing bug (see F-1736, job J-1235) but on the citation-extraction side rather than the threshold side -- worth a look together. Not fixed here (out of this job's scope, and skill code shouldn't be hand-edited mid-unrelated-job); flagging per CLAUDE.md rule 5 instead of silently dropping it or derailing to patch it.

plan_liveness.py's THRESHOLD_RES regex #2 (r"~?\s*(\d+)\+\s*(?:events|samples|rows|trials|cycles)\b") has no word/comma boundary check before the digits, so it can match mid-way through a larger comma-formatted number and silently produce a wrong, too-small threshold. Concrete real case (job J-1235, F-1736): docs/staged/geometry_tuple_index.md §1 reads "moments.jsonl (128MB, 14,210+ rows)" -- a plain description of moments.jsonl's own current size, not a threshold statement at all -- but re.search starts matching at the "2" right after the comma (since \d+ can't span the comma), producing a spurious match "210+ rows" -> n=210. This single wrong number then gets applied via parse_threshold()'s whole-doc fallback as THE promotion bar for every one of the plan's evidence files (six files in this case, none of which the plan actually states a bar for), inflating six real ACCRUING/STALE evidence files to false GATE-MET verdicts. This is a different failure mode than the "current count read as target" bug the SKILL.md's Known Limitations already documents and guards against with target-framed phrasing (n+/at least N) -- this phrasing genuinely IS target-shaped ("N+ rows"), the bug is that the captured N is a fragment of an unrelated, larger, comma-formatted number, not the number a human reading the sentence would ever read as "210". A fix could require the character immediately before the matched \d+ to not be a digit or comma (e.g. a negative lookbehind, or strip/normalize thousands-commas before matching, or require whitespace/sentence-start immediately before the number). Not fixed here (out of this job's scope); flagging per CLAUDE.md rule 5. See also S-0171 (filed same session, job:J-1235) for a related but distinct citation-extraction false positive on the same plan.
resolved_why: Fixed 2026-09-24 as part of the same THRESHOLD_RES rewrite as S-0143 -- see its own resolution. The exact reported case (geometry_tuple_index's '14,210+ rows' -> spurious 210, and a second instance -> spurious 16600 from a cross-bullet cue-word leak caught during this fix's own review) both verified gone from the live report; geometry_tuples.jsonl now correctly shows threshold '--'.

text: _emoji_window()'s CHAR_CAP=80 can silently degrade roadmap_hits() to emoji=None instead of flagging a real mismatch, if a badge's explanatory prose pushes the STAGE_EMOJI character more than 80 chars from the plan-link match position. Hit this live on J-1245 (euclidean_memory_plan): my first fix wrote a ~150-char correction note between the badge and the link on ROADMAP.md's own section-6.5 header line, and roadmap_hits() came back None instead of the new emoji -- not a crash, just silent under-detection (resolve_stage() then falls through to doc/memory priority with no ⚠, which happens to read as "no mismatch" even when ROADMAP's own badge is real and correct, purely because CHAR_CAP couldn't reach it). Confirmed by direct testing against plan_index.py's own functions before and after shortening the prose. Two independent fixes worth considering, either fixes it: (1) widen CHAR_CAP for headings that use `### ` (only `## ` is in _BOUNDARY_RE's early-stop pattern today -- a `###`-level heading's own window can run the full 80 chars in each direction even when the heading is short, but a wordy `###` line like this one still overflows it), or (2) have roadmap_hits() log a soft warning (not just return None) when a match position exists but the window scan found zero STAGE_EMOJI chars anywhere nearby, so a future stage-badge-sync pass can tell "no badge near this link" apart from "badge is just outside the window" instead of both reading identically as an unremarkable None. Not fixed here -- out of scope for J-1245's own badge-sync fix, and the actual badge in this case was moved closer to the link instead, which resolved it for this one row.

J-1148 (plan dream_overhaul, F-1755): this job's dispatched ground rules included "NEVER write under C:\Nascence\data" stated as a blanket, no-exception rule (grouped with "NEVER restart Du/the supervisor/any hub" and "NEVER flip a flag in scripts\life_flags.py"). Taken literally, this is in real tension with the SAME dispatch's own "ISOLATION REQUIRED" instruction to use lab_env.py's isolate() before any live-adjacent call -- isolate() itself always writes its lab dir under C:\Nascence\data\_lab\<timestamp>\ (confirmed by reading lab_env.py directly: `_LAB_ROOT = _ROOT / "data" / "_lab"`), and that subtree is the ONE explicitly allow-listed part of data/ the write-fence (core/profile.guard_path, D-0179/D-0200) treats as already-isolated -- i.e. it is the SANCTIONED way to touch anything data-adjacent for a lab job, not an exception that needs separate permission. A second, real gray zone: established scripts in this exact job chain (e.g. scripts/dream_exp_a_judge_shadow.py) have a designed, non-isolated, permanent default output path under data/logs/ (an instrument/shadow log, not live Du state, not gated by guard_path) -- a prior session (J-1125) reasoned this specific write was safe and used the live default path; this session's own ground rules gave no carve-out for that reasoning, so I redirected that one script's output to my own scratchpad via its --out flag instead (documented as a deliberate deviation in F-1755), leaving the canonical shared log incomplete until a future session's rules permit merging it in.

Suggestion: when job-run assembles a job group's ground rules, have the "NEVER write under C:\Nascence\data" line (or whichever generates it) either (a) explicitly except data/_lab/ (isolate()'s own sanctioned subtree) and name the data/logs/ shadow-log case as a judgement call rather than leaving it ambiguous, or (b) if the intent really is a hard, no-exception rule for a specific run (e.g. because Du is live and the group wants zero risk that run), say so explicitly enough that a session doesn't have to reverse-engineer whether isolate() itself is still allowed -- as currently phrased it reads as absolute but cannot literally be, since the same dispatch mandates isolate() elsewhere. Either fix removes a real ambiguity a session otherwise has to resolve by judgement call each time, inconsistently across sessions (my own resolution: isolate()'s own data/_lab/ writes are the sanctioned exception; a script's own non-isolated data/logs/ default output path is not, so I redirected it via --out instead of using the live default).

Lab dispatch scripts built against job-queue's own isolation convention (e.g. scripts/lab_j1205_scope_repair.py, scripts/lab_j1240_tiebreak_seat.py in C:\Nascence) each hand-roll a hub-reachability probe before --run, but only gate on the NEW/candidate hub, not on every hub the run will actually call. Suggestion: lab_env.py (or a new small sibling helper) could offer a standard "probe every hub this run will call, report all of them, and let the caller decide whether to proceed" pattern, so a job's own --run doesn't need to remember to gate on hubs it did not just add. The job-run dispatch skeleton's Setup phase creates worktrees under <scratch-root>/wt_<key> (worktree_dispatch.py::cmd_create: wt_dir = _state_dir(scratch_root).parent / f'wt_{key}'), where scratch-root is the dispatching session's own per-session scratchpad path -- never a fixed repo path. A dispatch script that hardcodes a guessed path like C:\Nascence\.claude\worktrees\wt_<key> in each Tier-3 agent's own prompt (instead of threading the Setup phase's real agent() return value into each Dispatch-phase prompt) is wrong on every run, every key. In batch 5 (2026-09-24, wf_0e1ab0fe-cc4) this was caught cleanly every time -- 8 of 14 Tier-3 agents independently ran worktree_dispatch.py list / git worktree list to find their real path, and in 6 of those cases the agent had already made one edit directly in the shared C:\Nascence tree first, caught it via git diff before staging, and self-corrected with a plain inverse Edit (never a banned git command) -- zero actual damage, but real wasted work repeated 6 times in one batch. Fix: the orchestrating session should pass setupResult (or at minimum the scratch-root value) into each runTier3Group()/runTier2Job() prompt string, so agents get the real path directly instead of a wrong guess plus a 'confirm if unsure' hedge that only some agents will front-load before their first edit.

The regex-based bool-vs-why coherence check (EXPL/NEG patterns in analyse(), shared with lab_j1205_scope_repair.py) was tuned against granite/JUDGE_1-style phrasing during earlier jobs in this plan (F-1280/F-1321). J-1261's full-N run (F-1850) found it matches ZERO of gemma4:12b's 144 arm-c why-texts (144/144 land in ambiguous_or_no_regex_match), even though gemma's own bool answers are highly accurate against the panel/battery (OVERALL_PASS=True). The instrument can confirm WHAT a candidate model answered but not corroborate WHY for a model whose explanation phrasing differs from granite's -- worth widening the regex (or adding a per-model phrasing profile) before the next candidate-model characterization in this plan relies on the coherence column to mean anything.

job-run's Tier 3 dispatch has no mechanical way to see a job's own embedded "do not pick up before <date>" scoping text -- it just dispatches whatever's open/ready. This chain (J-1140 -> J-1149 -> J-1223 -> J-1287 -> J-1299, the peer_correspondence_plan gate-1/gate-2 re-check on D-0207) is calendar-gated: the job's own briefing says "do not pick up before ~2026-09-27" because marcus's letter cadence (gap_days=8.0) means no new evidence can possibly exist before then. J-1287 checked 2026-09-24T07:20:59+12:00, found nothing changed, spawned J-1299 with the same "not before 2026-09-27" note -- and job-run's very next Tier 3 batch picked up J-1299 only 4.15 hours later, same calendar day, and (correctly, per this chain's own established precedent of always doing the fresh check even when picked up early) found the identical zero-change result again (F-1854). If job-run keeps dispatching same-day, this chain could churn a fresh successor job (and a fresh F-number) daily with zero new information for the ~3 days until 2026-09-27, and this same failure mode would hit any other calendar/cadence-gated job in the backlog, not just this one. Suggest: job_queue.py add/spawn gain an optional --not-before <ISO date> field, surfaced in `list`/`next` output and respected (skipped, not dispatched) by job-run's own tiering pass until that date arrives -- rather than relying on each picking-up session to notice and honor prose buried in the briefing text.

Verified end-to-end in an isolated scratch store (33 checks, all pass, no live store touched) before applying anywhere real. Applied retroactively to the actual job that prompted this (J-1333, peer_correspondence_plan, deferred to 2026-09-27T00:00:00+12:00 -- the literal date this chain's own briefings have cited since J-1299) -- confirmed via a fresh job_run.py plan that it dropped out of Tier 3 and now shows correctly in the new DEFERRED section (56.4h until due). This does not build S-0176's own separate, larger suggestion (a plan-declared shadow-promotion spec so a cheap generic check answers "has this gate fired" instead of a full job dispatch) -- that remains open as its own, bigger initiative.

Noticed in passing while working J-1305 (data_store_hygiene): job_queue.py's `session` field is set at job-creation time (who spawned it) and is never overwritten by `start`/`done` -- fine by itself, but J-1210's own record (`job_queue.py show J-1210`) carries "session": "8d915dfa-80f4-4aad-a2e3-206e842f08dd", a scratchpad-derived UUID, not a job ID like "J-XXXX". Tier 1/2 dispatch has no rule against a job's own commit including the ledger .jsonl files (docs/decisions.jsonl, findings.jsonl, job_queue.jsonl, session_events.jsonl, plan_snapshots.jsonl, skill_suggestions.jsonl, thoughts.jsonl) alongside its real file changes. In batch 7 (2026-09-24, wf_512c91be-649), J-1318's Tier1 commit (06c8de28) correctly applied the F-1549 same-file commit-safety recipe to findings.jsonl/job_queue.jsonl/session_events.jsonl (safely splicing in only its own added lines via the index-only recipe, verified HEAD-unchanged before committing) -- so no data was lost or clobbered -- but this means those 3 ledger files are now part of an unrelated commit's history ('J-1318: add missing __main__ guard...'), which Tier 3's own worktree_dispatch.py merge-back explicitly REFUSES to allow for exactly this reason (its own docstring: 'a legitimate agent should never produce one via git in the first place, since CLAUDE.md's own hand-edit ban already routes every real ledger write through its owning tool, which bypasses git entirely'). Tier 1/2 has no equivalent guard. Fix: add an explicit instruction to the Tier 1/2 dispatch prompt template -- when committing your own file changes, never git add the ledger .jsonl files even if they show as modified; those are tool-owned and get committed only via an explicit, separate, user-requested snapshot (same intent as Tier 3's hardcoded refusal, just not yet stated for Tier 1/2).

job_queue.py's own `start` and `done` subcommands accept a `--session` flag and correctly pass it through to the live event log (`ct.log_event(..., session=a.session)`, so job_started/job_done rows in docs/session_events.jsonl are attributed right), but neither command ever writes that value onto the job row's own `session` field in job_queue.jsonl. Read cmd_start (job_queue.py lines 259-267) and cmd_done (270-278): both only set `status` and `started`/`done_at`, never `r["session"] = a.session`. Confirmed live, not just from reading the source: after running `job_queue.py start J-1321 --session J-1321`, `job_queue.py show J-1321` still reported `"session": "J-1313"` (the session that had spawned J-1321 as a successor), not J-1321 itself. The job row's `session` field is therefore only ever set once, at `add`/`spawn` time (job_queue.py line ~125, `"session": session`), and never reflects who is actually working the job afterward -- only the separate session_events.jsonl log has the real per-action attribution. Low severity (the event log is authoritative and correct), but the job row's own `session` field is silently misleading to anyone reading job_queue.jsonl directly (e.g. a future `job_queue.py list`/`next` consumer, or a human skimming the store) since it looks like a "who has this" field but is actually "who created this." Suggest either: (a) have cmd_start/cmd_done also update r["session"] = a.session when provided, so the field tracks current/last owner, matching the field name's obvious meaning; or (b) if the field is deliberately meant as immutable creator/origin, rename it to something like `spawned_by_session` or `created_by_session` to stop it reading as current ownership. Noticed in passing while running the peer_correspondence_plan gate re-check chain (J-1321), not investigated further -- out of scope for that job.

lab_env.isolate()'s D-0206 "delete the DB copy if unwritten" check can produce a false "unwritten" verdict under db="empty" mode when the code under test writes real rows through the redirected DB_PATH. Observed directly in J-1348's own isolated smoke test (verify_J-1348.py, scratchpad): the run used `isolate(also=[...], db="empty")`, wrote and successfully read back several real memory_edges rows (confirmed in-process: all 19 assertions passed, including SELECT-backed checks against those exact rows), yet on __exit__ lab_env printed "DB copy unwritten -- deleted after retry (attempt 2/4), previously PermissionError" and the lab dir's nascence.db is now genuinely gone with no -wal/-shm sidecar left either.

Root cause (inferred, not fully isolated in a minimal repro): core/memory/store.py's _connect() sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;` unconditionally on every connection (confirmed by direct read, store.py:134). lab_env._hash_file() only ever hashes the single path `self._db_path` (lab_dir/"nascence.db") -- it never accounts for a same-named `.db-wal`/`.db-shm` sidecar. If a WAL checkpoint back into the main file hadn't happened yet at the moment __enter__ captured `self._db_baseline`, real committed writes can sit only in `-wal` and never move the main file's own hash, so __exit__'s "unchanged" comparison reads a false negative -- then deletes the (only) file it checked, silently discarding real test-written data that the docstring promises to keep for inspection on any real change ("Changed -> left exactly as before... dir kept for inspection").

Impact: not a live-store safety issue (data/_lab/ stays the designated quarantine area regardless; nothing ever touched the real DB) -- but a caller who genuinely needed the WAL-mode written DB left behind for inspection (the tool's own stated contract) can silently lose it. Whether this reproduces with db="copy" mode (a real DB file already present, not freshly schema'd) is untested -- this suggestion only covers the db="empty" path actually exercised.

Possible fix directions (not scoped/verified here -- out of J-1348's own scope, flagging per CLAUDE.md rule 5 rather than derailing to fix it): (a) force a checkpoint (`PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) on the isolated connection before computing either hash, or (b) fold any existing `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar bytes into the hash/existence check alongside the main file, or (c) hash sooner (right after __enter__, before any real connection with WAL pragmas has been opened against that path) is already what happens -- the gap is on the __exit__ side, after real WAL-mode writes.

D-0206's "unwritten DB copy" auto-delete check in lab_env.py's isolate.__exit__ hashes only the main
nascence.db file to decide whether the code under test ever wrote through the redirected DB_PATH. Since
core/memory/store.py opens with PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, a small test that writes only a few rows (via
store_fragment) can commit entirely into the -wal sidecar file without SQLite ever auto-checkpointing
back into the main .db file before __exit__'s hash check runs -- so the main file hashes as byte-identical
to its post-init_db() baseline even though real rows were written and were correctly queryable the whole
time through the same connection path. Observed directly running J-1346's own isolated smoke test
(verify_J-1346.py, db="empty" mode): 5 store_fragment() calls landed and were confirmed via SELECT COUNT
mid-test, yet __exit__ printed "DB copy unwritten -- deleted after retry" for that same lab dir. Not a
correctness bug (the isolation/redirect itself is unaffected either way; a false "unwritten" read only
means the tiny DB copy + its -wal/-shm sidecars get deleted afterward instead of kept, which was harmless
here since nothing needed inspecting post-hoc) -- but it means a caller who DOES rely on inspecting the
kept DB copy after a WAL-mode isolate() block, expecting D-0206's "changed -> left for inspection"
promise to hold, could be silently surprised by an empty/deleted lab dir instead. A fix (not attempted
here, out of this job's own scope) would need to either checkpoint WAL into the main file (e.g.
`PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);` on the redirected connection, or via a fresh connection to db_path)
before hashing in __exit__, or hash the main file plus any sibling -wal/-shm files together.

job_queue.py's parse_not_before() treats a naive (no-tzinfo) --not-before datetime as UTC. Every job in the J-1079..J-1338 wall-clock re-check chain has instead been passing the LOCAL (NZST/NZDT) clock digits as a bare string (e.g. --not-before 2026-09-29T16:10:23 to mean 168h after a regime floor whose LOCAL time is 16:10:23) -- so the stored value silently becomes 2026-09-29T16:10:23+00:00, a real UTC instant that is 12-13h LATER than the humans' actual intended local instant. Net effect across this whole chain: every not_before in it has been firing about 12-13h later than the plan doc's own prose claims, not earlier -- a real but low-severity latent bug (extra delay, not premature firing). parse_not_before's own docstring already documents the fix: pass an explicit offset, e.g. 2026-09-29T16:10:23+12:00 (or +13:00 once NZDT is in effect) instead of a bare local-looking string. J-1355 (2026-09-25) used the explicit-offset form for its own spawn (J-1356: --not-before 2026-09-26T20:41:00+12:00) to sidestep this rather than perpetuate it, but did not change any of the chain's PRIOR stored not_before values (out of scope for that job) -- worth a deliberate decision (fix the historical values retroactively via job_queue.py defer? just adopt the explicit-offset convention going forward?) rather than leaving it to keep recurring silently. Full worked evidence: F-1913/F-1914 (this session), and job_queue.py's own parse_not_before()/is_due() functions (~line 116-140).
resolved_why: Fixed 2026-09-25: parse_not_before() now refuses a naive datetime-with-time-component outright instead of silently assuming UTC, closing the 12-13h-late bug for NZ callers going forward. A bare date is unaffected. See F-1915 for full verification detail; SKILL.md's Deferral section updated with the new convention.

Suggestion: give plan_compact.py a `--fold-heading REGEX` (or similar) option that folds the first/only H2 section whose heading matches an arbitrary caller-supplied regex instead of hardcoding CS_HEAD -- same safety model (dry-run default, id audit, git-dirty check, atomic writes, session event), just parameterized on heading match. 1) A blind "later callout supersedes earlier callout in the same subsection" heuristic would have been WRONG here if applied mechanically to a sibling case: `### Improvement 1` has three stacked dated callouts (EVIDENCE REVIEW 2026-07-05, ENACTED 2026-07-05, BUILD STATUS 2026-07-01, in that document order, i.e. non-chronological) that look structurally identical to the Improvement-2 pair, but on a close read the BUILD STATUS callout's own decoupled-rater promotion criterion ("a decoupled rater... confirms... cleaner & more committed, not hedgier") is REAFFIRMED, not superseded, by a later "Sharpened promotion gate" section elsewhere in the same subsection ("That 'cleaner-not-hedgier' judgment... is the gate"). plan_state.py (and decide.py/findings_log.py/job_queue.py -- anything under _plan_tools_common with
ROOT = Path(r"C:\Nascence") hardcoded) always reads/writes the SHARED C:\Nascence tree, never a
job-run worktree's own copy of the same plan doc. job-run's own worktree-per-plan model (each job
edits docs/staged/<slug>.md via Edit/Write inside its own worktree, per CLAUDE.md's own ground
rules) means a job that both (a) rewrites a plan doc's design prose in its worktree and (b) calls
plan_state.py note/set on the same slug silently forks the doc into two diverging copies -- the
worktree's Edit-tool changes never reach the shared tree, and the shared tree's plan_state.py
writes (Current State bullets, Status/stage updates from OTHER sibling jobs on the same plan) never
reach the worktree. Found live in J-1429 (memory_as_a_service): by the time this job finished its
own sec4 rewrite, the shared tree already had 3 sibling jobs' worth of Current-State bullets
(F-2057/2061/2062, from J-1424/1425/1428, all on the SAME worktree/branch) that this job's own
worktree copy -- read at job start -- did not have, because those jobs' plan-doc updates went
straight to the shared tree via plan_state.py, bypassing the worktree entirely even though their
CODE commits landed on the shared branch. Reconciled manually this time (copied the shared tree's
current content into the worktree, re-applied the sec4 diff on top, re-committed) but nothing
catches this automatically, and a job that skips the check would silently lose either its own design
rewrite or the sibling jobs' Current-State history on the next merge. Possible fixes worth
considering (not scoped/prioritized here, just surfaced): plan_state.py could accept an optional
--root so a job-run worktree can point it at its own copy instead of the shared tree; or job-run's
own per-job briefing template could explicitly warn "diff your worktree's plan doc against the
shared tree's copy before your own plan_state.py note call, and reconcile if they've diverged" the
way this job's own ground rules already warn about git stash's shared-tree risk.

job_queue.py's own job record keeps a top-level "session" field that is set once at spawn time (to whichever session created the job, e.g. the spawning job's id) and is NOT updated by `start` or `done` to the session that actually did the work. Noticed on J-1648: I ran `start J-1648 --session J-1648` and `done J-1648 --session J-1648`, and both calls correctly logged job_started/job_done events tagged session "J-1648" in docs/session_events.jsonl (the real, authoritative trail) -- but `job_queue.py show J-1648` afterward still prints "session": "J-1625" (the session that originally spawned J-1648), which looks at a glance like my start/done session value never took, or like J-1625 did the work. It is harmless once you know to trust session_events.jsonl over the job record's own "session" field, but it cost a real detour this session chasing what looked like a lost-update race across concurrent job-run agents before the event log cleared it up (plus a UTC-vs-local-timezone read made the timestamps look stale too, compounding the confusion). Suggestion: either rename the job record's field to something like "spawned_by_session" to stop it reading as "current owner", or have `start`/`done` actually overwrite it with the --session value passed to that call, whichever better matches the tool's intent.

job_queue.py spawn has no --isolation flag (only add and list do), although the module docstring says a category=build job that needs a live-state repro should also set isolation=required. A build job spawned from a finding therefore always gets isolation=none (the default only flips to required for test and lab_experiment), and the only way to say otherwise is to fall back to add and lose spawn's --from provenance sugar, or to put an ISOLATION REQUIRED paragraph in the briefing text while the structured field stays none. Found while spawning J-1680 (a core/garden.py fix whose verification must run under lab_env.isolate()) from F-2252. Suggest: add --isolation none|required to the spawn subparser, and have spawn append the standard lab_env reminder whenever the resolved isolation is required (today it appends it only for kind test and lab_experiment).

plan_state.py cannot see docs/memory_levels_plan.md -- the same root-level legacy plan doc that decide.py's plan_exists() already trips on (S-0021, S-0048, S-0078, S-0080, S-0100, S-0105, all decide-side). find_plan()/all_plans() search only PLAN_DIRS = docs/plans, docs/staged, docs/shelf, so `plan_state.py note memory_levels_plan ...` exits with "no plan doc named memory_levels_plan.md under docs/plans, docs/staged or docs/shelf", and `show`/`lint`/`sync` likewise never see it. job-run's own ground rules tell every Tier-3 agent to record a plan note ONLY through plan_state.py note (and not to add a dated Current State section), so on this plan the sanctioned path is simply unavailable and each agent has to improvise a hand edit of a 263 KB doc (J-1271 annotated one stale bullet in place instead of regrowing a section). This plan is the most-linked one in the project (dozens of jobs, findings and decisions carry plan=memory_levels_plan), so it is exactly where the regrowth guard matters most, and it has no plan-state block, no Current State heading and is not covered by the lint/size-cap at all. Evidence: plan_state.py line 64 PLAN_DIRS, lines 106-111 find_plan; observed failure 2026-10-03 in J-1271 (exit message above); plan_sync_check.py reports the same file as "NOT a recognized plan location".

plan_compact.py --fold-bullets, run for real on lane2_the_witness (J-1551, F-2265), has two defects its dry-run table does not flag.

(1) Trailing-block swallow. bullet_spans() ends the document-order-last dated bullet only at the next H2/H3, so ALL undated content after it in the kept Current State section folds with that bullet. Here the oldest bullet's chunk was 3,047 B instead of about 600 B: 2,447 B of undated prose, three undated static bullets, an earlier "History folded" pointer and the "---" rule before section 0 all went into history too. Nothing is lost (verbatim in plan_history), but the live doc silently lost its static summary, the earlier pointer and the separator, and the dry-run table showed it only as one oddly large row. Suggested fix: end a dated bullet at the first blank line that is followed by a line that is not indented, not a dated bullet and not a list continuation; never fold a "> **History folded**" pointer or a bare "---" line; and print how many trailing undated lines were left in place.

(2) No dedupe against the existing history file. 12 of the 24 bullets folded were byte-identical to what an earlier fold (J-1570, 2026-09-28) had already appended to docs/plan_history/lane2_the_witness.md; consolidation commit 1ae5bb3 had re-added them to the live doc after that fold. --write appended about 13.7 KB of verbatim duplicates and the id audit cannot see it. Suggested fix: before folding, check each bullet's exact text against the history file, drop already-present ones from the live doc without re-appending them, and report "N already in history" in the dry-run.

S-0202 (the --fold-bullets idea) is still open; this is real-use evidence for it.

Refinement to S-0162 (promote live_since.py out of session scratchpads into the job-queue skill directory), from J-1070 (2026-10-03). When it is promoted, fix its unclean-boot close rule and the clock handling, both of which bit this run. (1) A boot with no 'Nascence shutting down.' line was closed at 'the last timestamped line before the NEXT awake line'; but a new process logs about 40 s of startup lines (the first is '[nascence.memory] Memory store initialised', then torchao/datasets/identity lines) BEFORE its '[nascence.main] Nascence is awake.' line, so that rule counts any dead gap as live: the 2026-09-30 20:28 boot (last real line 2026-10-01 07:17:42, then 47.6 h of silence) came out as 58.4 h instead of 10.8 h. (2) The log timestamps are naive local time; NZ DST began 2026-09-27 02:00 and the 2026-09-25 19:21 boot spans it, so naive subtraction over-counts that boot by 1.0 h; convert to UTC with zoneinfo Pacific/Auckland first. (3) Read the log only up to the size it had when opened, since Du appends.

pattern_discovery.py ranks pairs by the sum of rarity weights (1/ln(2+n_plans)) of the files two plans share, but never normalises by how many files each plan claims, so an inventory/catalog/umbrella plan scores high against every plan that owns one of its modules. Real evidence from J-0566's 2026-10-03 run (F-2269): of the top-40 --new-only pairs, 10 involve world_store_write_fence (an inventory plan: docs/staged/world_store_write_fence.md Inventory table, 29 core/ modules claimed, shared with 45 other plans, only 3 of which name it) and 7 of those were pure "both cite the same module" artifacts (reading how each doc actually uses the shared modules showed inventory rows, read-only citations or the same module simply being owned by the other plan, with no design coupling); 4 more involve antigravity_ecosystem_proposals (a 55-plan evaluation inbox) or udms_du_capability_trials (an umbrella index). Suggestion, in order of cost: (a) normalise the pair score by sqrt(deg_a * deg_b) (the node-strength normalisation the Serrano/Boguna/Vespignani disparity filter this tool is named after actually applies; today only the file-side weight is used), or (b) add --exclude-plan SLUG (repeatable) plus an automatic flag when one plan's claimed-file count exceeds N x the median, printing "inventory plan" next to its pairs, or (c) at minimum print each plan's claimed-file count beside every pair so a reader sees at a glance that a 146-edge plan is on one side. (a) needs a quick before/after read of the top 40 to make sure real pairs (e.g. the curiosity_goals_dreams<->curiosity_librarian_route and train_courier_cargo_ids<->train_split_merge links J-0566 found) do not fall below the cut.
resolved_why: Applied by J-1741 (F-2438): option (c) claimed-file counts printed beside every pair, and option (a) sqrt(deg_a*deg_b) normalisation as opt-in --normalise only. Not default because it buries F-2373's real links B/C (rank 69/81 -> 184/150) and promotes one-file-plan noise; the reviewed-pair store is what removes the repeated fence/antigravity/udms pairs.

text: pattern_discovery.py has no memory of which pairs a human or agent has already reviewed, so every re-run re-presents the same artifact pairs and each re-run repeats the same plan-doc reading. Real evidence: this review has now been filed three times (J-0226 on 2026-08-24, its stash row J-0386 wiped by the 2026-08-29 reset per F-0782, then J-0566 which sat in_progress ~27 days), and J-0566 re-read pairs such as emissary_lane2<->executive_world_grounding that F-0260 had already assessed. Suggestion: a small verdict store next to the edge store (C:\Users\USER\.claude\projects\C--Nascence\memory\_pattern_discovery_reviewed.jsonl, one row per pair: {pair, verdict: linked|incidental|inventory-artifact|already-linked, date, finding, shared_files_hash}) read by pattern_discovery.py; reviewed pairs are hidden by default (--show-reviewed to list them) and re-surface only when the pair's shared-file set changes (hash mismatch). The tool must keep its read-only-on-Nascence rule, so the store lives under the memory dir, not docs/. A companion `pattern_discovery.py review PLAN_A PLAN_B --verdict ... --finding F-XXXX` subcommand would make recording a verdict one line instead of prose in a finding.
resolved_why: Applied by J-1741 (F-2438): reviewed-pair store _pattern_discovery_reviewed.jsonl, hidden-by-default with hash re-surfacing, --show-reviewed, review and import-table subcommands, seeded from F-2373's 40-row table.

Noticed while closing J-1253 on docs/staged/ignition_pressure_and_time.md: plan_state.py note appends ONE dated bullet at the top of the kept Current State section and refreshes next/verified, but the older prose subsections under that same heading (### What we have / ### What we need / ### What we're doing next) stay exactly as they were, so after a note that reverses them the plan contradicts itself in one section. Here the new bullet says both gates were met and the read was done, while two lines below it the untouched text still says "J-1253 stays open/in_progress; re-check the restart gate each session until Du restarts onto da061f3 plus 5 live days" and "gate still NOT met". The note tool is the only sanctioned way to touch a plan doc after a job, and hand-editing the shared-tree doc is off limits to job-run agents, so the agent cannot fix the stale prose and the next reader has to know the top bullet wins.

Suggestion: add a sanctioned way to retire those subsections, either plan_state.py note --supersedes (strikes or folds the three prose subsections into plan_history and leaves only the new bullet), or plan_state.py rewrite SLUG --have/--need/--next (replaces just those three subsections, one line each, with the same atomic write and session event). At minimum, have note print a warning when the kept Current State section still carries a What we need / What we're doing next subsection older than the bullet it just added. Not fixed here (scope creep on a read-only analysis job and out of reach of the sanctioned tools).

job_run.py stale_in_progress() flags in_progress jobs by the age of their own started timestamp only, so it cannot tell a job that is genuinely waiting from one whose work is already DONE and was simply never closed. Concrete case, J-1536 (2026-09-27): a session started it at 19:21:51Z, recorded its answer F-2134 (finding session field = J-1536) at 19:31:51Z, spawned J-1571 (which later finished), and never ran job_queue.py done. The job then sat in_progress ~5 days, invisible to job-run's ready tiers, until a manual takeover found the work complete and only the plan-doc note and the close missing. Suggest adding one cheap signal to the STALE-LOOKING IN-PROGRESS rows: list any finding whose session field equals the job id (and any job whose spawned_from is such a finding), e.g. "F-2134 recorded 10 min after start, no done" -- a strong forgot-to-close marker that the orchestrator could surface or even propose done for. Noticed while doing J-1536; not changed here.

No amend or supersede command: findings are append-only, so correcting a small miscount in a recorded finding forces a whole new addendum finding (J-1450 had to record F-2306 to correct F-2303). A record --supersedes F-XXXX flag (linking the new row and marking the old one superseded in list/show) would keep one live claim per fact.

note has only --text, no --text-file, and its text must avoid quotes, backticks, dollar signs and apostrophes when passed inline in a shell; a long evidence-heavy note (the normal case after a review job) is awkward and error prone. A --text-file flag, like every other ledger tool here has, would fix it.

job_run.py plan rejects any trailing positional: a 2026-10-03 job-run workflow Refresh-phase computed the literal command 'job_run.py plan --json .' and argparse exited 2 ('job_run: error: unrecognized arguments: .') with EMPTY stdout, so a script that JSON-parses the agent's return would get nothing. The SKILL.md dispatch skeleton only says 'job_run.py plan --json (apply any limits given)', and '.' is not a limit flag, so the workflow author appended a stray argument that the skill's own docs never sanction. The subagent worked around it by running 'plan --json' (the plan subparser never reads a path; the store root is fixed internally via common.ROOT) and returning that JSON, but could not flag the discrepancy because the required return format is JSON-only. Suggest one of: (a) give the plan subparser an optional ignored trailing root positional (nargs='?') so a bare repo path is harmless, or (b) make the SKILL.md skeleton explicit that ONLY --tier1-limit/--tier2-limit/--tier3-limit/--stale-days/--udms-check flags may be appended, so the workflow script cannot pass a bare path.

spawn has three rough edges seen while spawning J-1715 and J-1716 from J-1704: (1) spawn --from plan:SLUG records spawned_from but leaves the plan field null, so spawned jobs lose plan attribution, and spawn offers no --plan while add does; (2) spawn --kind test always sets isolation required with no flag to set none, even for a read-only grep job, whereas add has --isolation; (3) there is no edit or cancel subcommand, so a mis-flagged spawned job can only be duplicated or left as is. Suggest: spawn accepts --plan and --isolation and defaults plan from a plan:SLUG source, and a cancel subcommand that takes a reason.

Restart-gated jobs (about 25 open: J-1181, J-1182, J-1187, J-1192, J-1304, J-1455, J-1503, J-1544, J-1615 and more) each hand-roll a boot map from nascence.log in their own scratch script. When a briefing carries a restart gate, job-queue add and next could cite that command as the gate check and the booted-after bucket (with its live-hours) as the pass criterion, so the next reader neither re-derives the boot map nor treats a commit time as the time a change went live.

_plan_tools_common/common.py: load_edges(path=EDGES_PATH) and save_edges(edges, path=EDGES_PATH) bind their default path when the module is imported. So a harness that dry-runs build_edges.main() "on a copy" by assigning ct.EDGES_PATH = <scratch copy> redirects ONLY the lock file and a cosmetic print: main() still loads the REAL store and save_edges() still OVERWRITES the real store. Found while building J-1684's verification harness (I had to rebind ct.load_edges.__defaults__ and ct.save_edges.__defaults__ by hand and md5-check the real store before and after to be safe). Every job briefing that says "test on a copy / dry mode" for build_edges walks into this. Suggestion: make both defaults path=None resolved to EDGES_PATH at call time, or give build_edges.main() an optional edges_path argument plus a dry_run flag that skips save_edges and log_event. Also stale in memory-links/SKILL.md: "Re-running build_edges.py is safe - it dedupes ... and only adds what's new" predates the 2026-08-23 rebuild-from-scratch change (the module docstring says REBUILD, not backfill).

findings_log show rejects --session while record accepts it, so a blanket instruction to pass --session on every findings-log call errors on show; accept and ignore --session on show and list for consistency

Second call site of S-0250: the same 2026-10-03 job-run workflow's Plan-phase task computed the literal command 'job_run.py plan .' (plain-text mode, no --json; task text: 'From cwd C:\Nascence, run: python job_run.py plan . Return its exact text output verbatim, nothing added.'). argparse exited 2 ('job_run: error: unrecognized arguments: .') exactly like S-0250's 'plan --json .' variant, so BOTH calls in the workflow script append the stray '.', not just the Refresh-phase one. Fixing only the --json call site would leave this one failing. The subagent worked around it by running 'job_run.py plan' (the documented form in SKILL.md's 'The three tiers' block; the plan subparser never reads a path, the store root is fixed internally via common.ROOT) from cwd C:\Nascence and returning that text, and did not flag the discrepancy in its return because the required return format was 'verbatim, nothing added'. S-0250's two fixes both cover this call site too: (a) give the plan subparser an optional ignored trailing root positional (nargs='?'), or (b) make SKILL.md explicit that only the limit/--stale-days/--udms-check flags may be appended. Either way the workflow script itself should also stop passing '.' on both calls.

job-queue briefings that carry "ISOLATION REQUIRED" are applied uniformly, even to pure read-only measurement jobs (log / jsonl reads plus an SQLite SELECT). For those, lab_env.isolate() is the wrong tool: it copies the ~877 MB live nascence.db and leaves a data/_lab/<timestamp>/ directory in the live tree, while a read-only reader (sqlite "file:...?mode=ro&immutable=1", no core.* imports, and a stat of nascence.db / -wal / -shm before and after as the backstop) cannot write at all and is much cheaper. Suggest a documented "read-only reader" branch in lab_env.py's docstring and job-queue SKILL.md (and a spawn-time hint when kind=test and the briefing only says "read"), so an agent does not have to decide ad hoc whether skipping isolate() is allowed. Noticed during J-1400 (F-2358); J-1400 used the read-only path and recorded identical before/after DB stat.

plan_state.py note takes --text only (no --text-file / --next-file), but a Related backfill note must contain backticked slug.md references for build_edges.py to harvest - exactly the characters CLAUDE.md and the bash-backtick memory say to keep out of shell arguments. J-1723 had to drive the CLI from a Python subprocess to pass five such notes. Add --text-file and --next-file the way findings_log/decide/job_queue have their --*-file flags.

atomic_write_text in the shared plan-tools common module raised PermissionError on os.replace when another agent held the ledger open (seen on a findings_log record during a busy job-run wave); a short retry with backoff inside atomic_write_text would stop the first-call failure that agents currently retry by hand

job-queue has no way to amend an open job's briefing, so a briefing written before its prerequisite landed goes stale. Example from J-1722: J-1679 (the D-0278 netting re-check) says "if the observability log line from the queued build job has landed, that line", but once J-1722 built it there was nowhere to attach "it landed as F-2386, grep nascence.log for bed-exposure, and read zero lines as not shown, not as unused". The only workaround was the plan-state next line, which a job-run agent may not read before it starts the job. Suggest a small `job_queue.py note J-XXXX --text-file F` that appends a dated, session-stamped addendum to the briefing (kept separate from the original text so the history stays readable), and that `show` / `next` print it under the briefing, so a build or finding that closes a dependency can point its waiting successor at the new instrument.

﻿lab_env.isolate() redirects only core.memory.store.DB_PATH (plus any also= globals). A lab/test that calls core.model_client.call_node (directly, or through core.peers.compose_letter and similar) ALSO appends to llm_calls.jsonl, llm_latency.jsonl and thought_station_log.jsonl in the LIVE data/ dir via core.telemetry's three writers, unless the process calls core.telemetry.enter_lab_mode() (D-0252) before its first call. Neither lab_env.py's docstring, job-queue SKILL.md's isolation section, nor the lab_env reminder that spawn appends to test/lab_experiment briefings mentions this, so a model-calling lab that follows the instructions to the letter still leaks live telemetry rows. Suggest one paragraph in lab_env.py's module docstring and in SKILL.md ("model-calling labs: also telemetry.enter_lab_mode(); see scripts/lab_isolation.py neutralize_telemetry()"), or an isolate(telemetry=True) option. J-1668 did it by hand (scripts/lab_j1668_hub_cold_warm_probe.py: enter_lab_mode() before any call).

lab_env: a worktree based build must import lab_env first, because importing it puts the main Nascence tree at the front of sys.path, and only then put its own worktree path in front before importing core, or the main tree core shadows the code under test. Tests that import core modules were also refused by the auto mode classifier until they ran under isolate. Suggest a lab_env command, run WORKTREE SCRIPT, that does the import order, wraps the script in isolate with an empty db, and hashes the live data files before and after; J-1733 hand rolled exactly that in a scratch wrapper.

A queued job's briefing cannot be amended or annotated after a founder ruling changes its premise (the CLI has only add, spawn, list, next, show, start, done, defer): J-1711 was filed while D-0340 was open and its invariant (b) is now stale once D-0340 is built, so the only fix is a finding plus a plan note that the future executor must happen to read. A job_queue.py note or amend command that appends a dated addendum to the briefing and shows in show and next would close that gap.

decide.py has no way to mark a ruled decision as closed or superseded by a later one. D-0272 (wire fix (b) as a shadow) had its defeater (b) met by F-2309; D-0336 was opened and ruled End the shadow as the answer and J-1765 built it, yet D-0272 still reads as a plain ruled decision with an empty history and no link to D-0336, and its defeater text still looks live to any scan. Only open, rule, reopen, set-plan, list and show exist, and rule and reopen overwrite or re-open the founder ruling with no guard, so an agent that wants the ledger tidy has no safe call. plan_compact.py's plain dry-run line "nothing to fold ... N dated bullet(s) past --keep 1; try --fold-bullets" can point at the wrong text. lab_env.py (job-queue skill) shadows the caller's own core package: lines 144-145 do sys.path.insert(0, "C:\Nascence") on import, so after `import lab_env` any `import core...` resolves to the SHARED tree even when the test was launched from a job-run worktree (verified by experiment, see the finding on the 2026-10-04 second leak). Effects: isolate()-using tests run from a worktree (a) exercise master's code instead of the branch under test and (b) write Du's LIVE data through every module not named in isolate(also=[...]) (2026-10-04 16:49:37: five live files polluted via core.prediction_error / shadow_integrity / core.satisfaction while Du was down; repaired by the orchestrator). Suggested fix: append instead of insert(0) (or insert only when `core` is not importable from the caller's tree), keep `from core.memory import store` working for callers outside C:\Nascence, add a one-line log of which core tree isolate() resolved, and document the caveat in job-queue's SKILL.md and job-run's worktree section (the rule 'run tests from your worktree' is not sufficient for isolate-using tests until this is fixed). Optional hardening: while an isolate() block is open, an audit-hook tripwire that records any write-mode open under the live data/ outside the lab dir.
resolved_why: Applied by the job-run orchestrator on 2026-10-04 (urgent: the shadowing caused a live-store leak the same day, F-2423). lab_env.py now appends C:/Nascence to sys.path instead of inserting it at position 0 (backup lab_env.py.bak_F-2423_orchestrator_20261004). Verified: the experiment now shows a fake worktree's core still resolves to the worktree after import lab_env; a caller outside any Nascence tree still resolves core through the appended path; new regression test scripts/_test_lab_env_core_resolution.py passes 10 of 10 checks on the fixed file and fails the three F-2423 checks against the pre-fix copy. safe_commit.py leaves the shared .git/index entry for a path it commits stale (for a --new-file path the index shows 'D ' plus an untracked copy; for an existing path the index keeps the old blob). worktree_dispatch.py merge-back then refuses EVERY branch with 'local changes would be overwritten' even though disk == HEAD. (2) The dispatch ground rules should forbid killing processes by PID or window title; a lab agent ran a wildcard WINDOWTITLE taskkill to stop its own script (F-3067).

lab_env.isolate() hardcodes _LAB_ROOT to C:\Nascence\data\_lab, so every hermetic harness run from a throwaway worktree still creates directories (and copies the live DB) under the LIVE data/ tree while Du is up. Suggest: isolate() derives its lab root from the repo the caller imported core from (core.__file__), or takes an explicit lab_root argument, with the live-tree default only when cwd is C:\Nascence itself. Also a sweeper for the empty 20261030_* dirs (D-0242).

A --since-boot evidence gate pins since_ts to the boot current at defer time, so a successor read whose evidence can only exist AFTER THE NEXT restart (the build it reads is merged but restart-gated) reads as met at once on the current boot: J-2597 (needs Du down; ignition_log 1 row = 53/1), J-2610 (needs a second boot; monologue_log 800 = 1538/800), J-2611 (night_log 1 row, already met), J-2603 (p2 shadow 10 rows, 4 of them from the OLD code). Four cases in waves 10-12 on 2026-10-30. Suggest a gate predicate that names the evidence directly: --gate-boot-after <git commit> (met only when Du's boot_ts is newer than that commit's merge into master) and/or --gate-du-down (met only when no hot-model port answers), so lab jobs and post-merge reads stop needing a hand-held list in the handoff.

plan-index's stage-mismatch detector compares the plan-state block's stage vocabulary (shipped, superseded, live, built) against ROADMAP emoji badges and the Status line, so it keeps re-filing a sync job for plans that already agree: J-2583 (6 plans) found only cat_overhaul genuinely stale and closed, and the very next plan-maintain run filed J-2616 for the same remaining 5 (factory_candidates_from_history, generative_world_sedimentation, spatial_perception, question_cargo, world_store_write_fence). Suggest: map plan-state stages onto the emoji legend before comparing (shipped/live -> the live badge, superseded -> the retired badge, built -> building), or treat the block as authoritative since the J-1485 migration and only flag ROADMAP badges that disagree with the MAPPED stage.

defer --live-hours counts hours summed since a fixed anchor, so on J-2541 (14 live days AFTER the D-0509 floor lands at the next boot) it read 1309.3/336 the moment it was set and would not hold the job at all. A gate of the form "N live hours after <gate-file match lands>" (anchor = the matched row's timestamp, or the first boot after it) is what post-change reads need; today the only fallback is a calendar not_before, which the job-gates rule (feedback_job_gates_evidence_not_time) says to avoid.

Two rough edges seen on J-2611: (1) a since_boot gate stamped before a code merge reads as due even though the code the read is about never ran; a gate form like boot-after-commit (or since_ts re-stamped on defer) is needed. (2) defer on an in_progress job sets the gate but leaves status in_progress, so a deferred job is not reopened; there is no reopen command and hand-editing the jsonl is forbidden.
